artists.biography:
The Black Crowes are an American rock band formed in 1989. Their discography includes nine studio albums, four live albums and several charting singles. The band was signed to Def American Recordings in 1989 by producer George Drakoulias and released their debut album, Shake Your Money Maker, the following year. The follow-up, The Southern Harmony and Musical Companion, reached the top of the Billboard 200 in 1992.

After a hiatus between 2002 and 2005, the band released Warpaint, which hit number 5 on the Billboard chart. After the release of a double album, the greatest hits-like and mostly acoustic Croweology in August 2010, the band started a 20th anniversary tour that was followed by an ongoing second hiatus.

The band has opened for various rock acts such as Heart, Robert Plant, Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers, the Dave Matthews Band, the Grateful Dead, Aerosmith and ZZ Top, and performed live with Jimmy Page and Oasis, among others. The band has sold over 30 million albums, and is listed at number 92 on VH1's "100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock". They were also labeled by Melody Maker as "The Most Rock 'n' Roll Rock 'n' Roll Band in the World" and the readers of Rolling Stone voted them 'Best New American Band' in 1990.

perplexity.description:
Shake Your Money Maker Live is a double live album by The Black Crowes, originally released in 2023 on the Silver Arrow label. The album captures the band performing their debut studio album, Shake Your Money Maker, in its entirety on the first disc, followed by a second disc featuring live renditions of other Black Crowes classics and a cover of The Rolling Stones' "It's Only Rock 'n Roll (But I Like It)." Musically, the album showcases the band's signature blend of blues rock, southern rock, and roots rock, delivered with the high-energy, raw sound that has defined their live shows for decades.

As the first live album to present the full debut album in concert, Shake Your Money Maker Live holds a unique place in The Black Crowes' discography, marking both a celebration of their origins and a testament to their enduring live prowess. The release was well-received by fans and critics alike, praised for its faithful yet vibrant performances and the palpable connection between the band and their audience. The album stands as a powerful document of The Black Crowes' legacy as one of rock's most dynamic live acts.
